newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midcontinent diesel fuel prices rise.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midcontinent diesel fuel prices rise.

text.p: U.S. Midcontinent diesel fuel prices firmed on surging NYMEX heating oil futures and steady differentials in Chicago and Group Three Wednesday, traders said.
NYMEX heating oil hit a post-Gulf War high of 72.90 cents a gallon midday on reports of historically low distillate inventories before falling back on profit taking.

In the Midwest, diesel fuel differentials were largely unchanged despite a 624,000 barrel build in Midwest distillate stocks that left inventories in the region about 3,000 barrels above the same week last year, traders said.
American Petroleum Institute late Tuesday said Midwest refineries were operating at 97.2 percent of capacity last week, down 2 percentage points on turnarounds and an outage at regional refineries.
Group Three low sulphur diesel firmed to bids 0.25 cent a gallon over the print for prompt October deliveries and even with the print for later deliveries, traders said.
Chicago prompt low sulphur made a similar upward move to bids 0.25 cent a gallon over the print, with later deliveries even with the print.
High sulphur was steady in both markets at 2.0/1.75 cents a gallon under the print.
Unleaded gasoline differentials were unchanged in Chicago and Group Three.
